Definition: Laban, a Mesopotamian; also a place in the Desert
BiblicalUsage: Laban is Jacob's uncle and father-in-law, the Syrian of Padan-aram who gave Jacob his wives and cheated him of his wages. In Genesis 24:29 he runs out to meet Abraham's servant at the well, in Genesis 24:50 he and Bethuel agree the marriage "proceedeth from the LORD," and in Deuteronomy 1:1 the same name marks a place in the wilderness, a different Laban from the man.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that Laban is the picture of the man who bargains with God and loses: he served the Lord's purpose for Jacob and Rebekah, and he could not keep Jacob from the blessing.
